genZNote: Multidrug-resistant, hard to identify with routine methods, and stubbornly persistent on hospital surfaces — everything you don't want in an outbreak organism.

morphology.notes: Often reclassified taxonomically as Candidozyma auris; still commonly referred to clinically as Candida auris. Forms clusters of budding cells, usually without true hyphae or pseudohyphae

habitat.naturalHabitat: Not well characterized in nature; thought to have emerged from a wetland/estuarine environmental niche
habitat.hostAssociation: Colonizes human skin; opportunistic pathogen in hospitalized/long-term care patients
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Persists on hospital surfaces and equipment for extended periods, resisting many standard disinfectants
habitat.reservoir: Human skin (colonization); contaminated healthcare surfaces and equipment

microscopy.appearance: Budding yeast cells, morphologically similar to other Candida species

culture.media: Sabouraud dextrose agar; CHROMagar Candida (variable, sometimes ambiguous color)
culture.growthCharacteristics: Grows at 37-42°C, tolerates higher salt concentrations than most Candida species
culture.colonyMorphology: Smooth, white to cream, sometimes pink colonies — not reliably distinguishable from other Candida species by colony appearance alone

identificationClues: Frequently misidentified as other Candida species (e.g. C. haemulonii) by standard biochemical panels
Requires MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry or molecular (PCR/sequencing) methods for reliable identification
Multidrug resistance across multiple antifungal classes is common
Persists on healthcare surfaces, driving outbreaks in hospitals and long-term care facilities

diseases: Colonization without infection in many patients
virulenceFactors: Biofilm formation on medical devices and surfaces
clinicalImportance.transmission: Healthcare-associated — spread via contaminated hands, equipment, and environmental surfaces; can persist for weeks on surfaces
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Emerged as a serious global public health threat; the CDC and WHO have designated it a critical priority pathogen due to multidrug resistance, difficulty of identification, and propensity for healthcare outbreaks
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Standard biochemical identification methods frequently misidentify it — designated an urgent public health threat requiring specialized identification and infection control measures

examFacts.keyBiochemicalReaction: Germ tube negative; requires MALDI-TOF/molecular ID
examFacts.importantTest: MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry or molecular sequencing (standard biochemical panels are unreliable)
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Frequently multidrug-resistant and persists on hospital surfaces far longer than most Candida species
